cassia.predicted_cell_type: Immune cell — cytotoxic lymphocyte / NK-lineage cell
strengths: Correctly identifies a cytotoxic lymphocyte program via GZMB, GZMH, KLRB1, KLRC1, CST7, IL2RB.
Avoids over-committing by leaving the label unmapped.
weaknesses: Label is not ontology-resolvable and confounds NK-lineage with T-cell evidence.
Discards or ignores branch-specific TCR evidence (TRBV27, TRAV2).
Fallback candidate CLIDs include biologically implausible non-immune cell types.

strengths: Supported by cluster-level TCR variable gene evidence TRBV27 and TRAV2.
Adaptive immune pathway enrichment (Class I MHC antigen processing/presentation) is consistent with T-cell identity.
Cytotoxic markers can be interpreted as an effector T-cell state rather than requiring NK identity.
weaknesses: The top2 refinement to effector CD8-positive alpha-beta T cell lacks direct positive CD8A/CD8B evidence.
Overall marker list is noisy with many non-canonical genes, and the in-house scores are low.

strengths: Detects the cytotoxic/NK-associated markers GZMB, GZMH, KLRB1, KLRC1, CST7, IL2RB.
weaknesses: Ignores positive TCR variable gene evidence (TRBV27, TRAV2) that favors T-cell over NK identity.
Overstates the discriminatory power of KLRB1/KLRC1, which are also expressed by T-cell subsets.
Reliance on absence of CD3/CD8 from a 50-gene top DEG list is not positive evidence for NK identity.

supporting: TRBV27 and TRAV2 are TCR variable genes present in the cluster DEG list and provide positive branch-specific evidence for T-cell over NK-cell identity.
GZMB, GZMH, KLRB1, KLRC1, CST7, IL2RB, and IFI16 support a cytotoxic effector lymphocyte phenotype consistent with effector T cells.
Reactome adaptive immune pathway enrichment (Adaptive Immune System
Class I MHC mediated antigen processing & presentation) supports adaptive T-cell identity (PMID 37397988).
conflicting: The top DEG list lacks classic CD3D/CD3E/CD8A/CD8B markers, which can be used to argue against conventional T cells but is not conclusive in a 50-gene top list.
KLRB1, KLRC1, GZMB, and GZMH are traditionally emphasized as NK markers and motivated the NK hypothesis, but they do not discriminate NK cells from cytotoxic T cells.
Several top DEGs (e.g., S100A1, SPX, TAS2R20, FSHR) are not canonical T/NK markers, adding noise to the cluster signature.
enrichment_or_literature: Reactome pathways from the dossier include Adaptive Immune System, Immune System, Interleukin receptor SHC signaling, and Class I MHC mediated antigen processing & presentation, consistent with an adaptive/cytotoxic lymphocyte identity.
